conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Hi, I'm Dr. Lee. I understand your G-tube clogged and you've been feeling really sick since then.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes, it clogged yesterday. I tried flushing it, but it ripped and stomach contents spilled out.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I see. That must have been distressing. You started having nausea, vomiting, and abdominal pain after that?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes, nonstop. I’ve lost count of how many times I’ve vomited. And now there’s this burning rash where the fluid touched my skin.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That sounds like irritation from the tube contents. We’ll clean it and start treatment. Any fever or chills?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: No, no fever. Just the pain and nausea.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good. Your vitals are stable. We’ve checked your labs and found your potassium is a bit low, so we’re giving you some IV fluids and potassium.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay. Will I be able to eat or feed through the tube soon?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Not yet. The tube is damaged, so we’ll need to replace it. The interventional radiology team will do that tomorrow.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Again? This is the second time in months.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I know it’s frustrating. We’ll use a larger tube this time to reduce the chance of clogging.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good morning. The team replaced your GJ tube this morning with a 16 French one. It’s now in the right place.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Is it safe to start feeds?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ll start slowly tomorrow. Your stomach needs time to adjust after the procedure.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: What about the rash? It still burns.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ve started a cream called betamethasone and an antibiotic ointment to prevent infection. It should improve in a few days.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’re starting your tube feeds today with a new formula called Osmolite 1.5. It’s easier on your stomach.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Will this one cause less nausea?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We hope so. We’ll go slow and monitor you closely. If you tolerate it, we’ll increase the rate.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Your stool test came back positive for C. difficile. That could be contributing to your nausea and loose stools.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Again? I had that before.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, it’s a recurrence. We’re starting oral vancomycin for 10 days to treat it.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Will that help me feel better faster?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, it should reduce the diarrhea and help your gut heal. We’ll keep monitoring your symptoms.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re doing well with the feeds. The vancomycin seems to be helping—your stools are less frequent.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: The rash is also less red. But I felt a gurgle in my tube this morning and then it stopped draining.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ll check it. Sometimes they can clog again, especially with formula changes.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I’m sorry, but the tube is clogged again. We’ll need to replace it.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Again? This is so discouraging.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I understand. We’ll use an 18 French tube this time—larger to prevent clogging. The team will do it tomorrow.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good news—the new 18 French tube was placed successfully. It’s working well.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Can we restart feeds?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, we’ll restart Osmolite 1.5 at a low rate and increase as you tolerate it.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re tolerating the feeds well. Your nausea has improved, and your labs are stabilizing.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That’s a relief. How long before I can go home?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: If this continues, likely in two days. We’ll finish your vancomycin course and make sure the tube stays open.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Will I need to keep using this new formula?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, we think Osmolite 1.5 is better for your gastroparesis. We’ll send it home with you.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Your rash is improving. We’ll keep using the creams for a few more days.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: The betamethasone says not to use it long-term. Is that safe?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good question. We’ll stop it after two weeks—it can thin the skin. The Bactroban will continue for infection prevention.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And the vancomycin?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’ll finish a 10-day course. We’re prescribing four more days to complete it at home.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re doing great. The tube is working, feeds are at goal, and your pain is controlled.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Can I go home tomorrow?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, if all goes well. We’ll finalize your discharge plan today.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Will I have help at home?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, home health will assist with wound care and tube management. They’ll teach your husband too.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: What about follow-up?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Gastroenterology and oncology will see you soon. We’ll send records and prescriptions.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good morning. You’re cleared to go home today.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’m so glad. Thank you for fixing the tube and helping me feel better.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re welcome. Remember: use the creams as directed, finish the vancomycin, and keep using Osmolite 1.5.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And flush the tube regularly?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Exactly. Flush with water before and after feeds and meds. Call if it clogs or the rash worsens.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I will. And I’ll keep my appointments.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Perfect. We’re also continuing your regular meds: omeprazole, metoclopramide, gabapentin, and pain meds as needed.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And Denosumab?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, resume your usual schedule. Oncology will manage that.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thank you for explaining everything.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re doing well. Take care, and call if anything changes.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I will. Thanks again.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: The discharge nurse will go over wound care and give you supplies.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay, I’m ready.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ll also send instructions on how to clean the skin around the tube and change the dressing daily.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Should I moisten the dressing before removing it?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, to avoid trauma. Use saline to dampen it first.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Got it.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: And keep monitoring for signs of infection: increased redness, swelling, or pus.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’ll watch for that.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’ve made great progress. We’re confident you’ll do well at home.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I feel much better than when I came in.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That’s the goal. Take it easy, follow the plan, and we’ll see you in follow-up.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I appreciate all your help.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re very welcome. Have a safe trip home.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thank you.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: One last thing—your husband can call the on-call team if he has questions about tube care.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: He’ll be glad to know that.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’re here to support you both.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That means a lot.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Rest well, and take care.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I will. Thank you.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re all set. The nurse will bring your discharge papers shortly.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay, I’m ready to go.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Take care, and we’ll see you in clinic soon.
